title: Pre-merge compatibility and package audit of packages/fw-agent at the v0.5.x release-blocker candidate (PR #73)
objective: RELEASE-001 audited packages/fw-agent as it stood at candidate_sha 94388bd, before the v0.5.x release-blocker work (F-69 through F-83) existed. This directive re-runs Team Configuration 4 against the CURRENT candidate (PR #73, commit 196cf3d) -- the state that would actually be tagged and published via .github/workflows/publish.yml's Trusted Publishing (OIDC) flow if the repo owner merges next. Confirms the package that would ship still passes the same eight compatibility dimensions and ten release-audit checks, and specifically that none of the F-69..F-83 fix work (extra SECURITY.md/CHANGELOG.md content, the new policy-watcher.js/behavior-tracker.js/index.js code, the regenerated .helios-baseline, the new sign-policy.js copy-loop logic) changed anything that would break a consumer or leak something into the published tarball that shouldn't be there.
base_sha_note: Same base_sha as RELEASE-001 (the last point this package was formally release-audited) -- this directive's real prior point of comparison is RELEASE-001's own candidate_sha (94388bd), noted here for continuity; base_sha is kept identical to RELEASE-001 rather than bumped to something mid-stream so the diff a reviewer inspects, if any, spans the same window RELEASE-001 established.
scope: packages/fw-agent's package.json, .npmignore (if present), README.md, LICENSE, and the real `npm pack --dry-run --json` output at candidate_sha 196cf3d
whether package.json's version (currently 0.5.0) and the engines/exports/files fields still hold given everything F-69..F-83 touched
whether .helios-baseline's regeneration (F-83's fix touched a hashed engine file) is correctly included in the packaged files list, matching what's declared in package.json's files array
out_of_scope: packages/fw-control -- not being prepared for a standalone npm release in this directive
actually running npm publish or any registry-modifying command -- audit only
.github/workflows/publish.yml itself -- a repo-level CI workflow, not part of the published npm package, and not something npm pack would include
success_criteria: compatibility-receipt.json reviews the eight dimensions against packages/fw-agent's current exports/engines/dependencies, explicitly comparing against RELEASE-001's prior findings where relevant (confirm nothing RELEASE-001 passed has since regressed)
release-audit-receipt.json's packaged_files is the real, verbatim npm pack --dry-run output at candidate_sha 196cf3d, not asserted and not copied from RELEASE-001's report
explicit answer to 'what would accidentally get packaged' -- even if the answer is nothing
explicit confirmation that .helios-baseline in the tarball matches the value committed in this PR (672ff05125f9db8ebb85a71c51e30160723f1ef03812fc4932ec4c9b13c6a4d4)
